intro: Both islands of New Zealand in eleven days. The glow-worm caves of Waitomo and two nights in Rotorua for geysers, kiwi and a Māori cultural evening, then a flight to Christchurch and a self-drive loop of the South Island: over the Southern Alps to the Franz Josef and Fox glaciers, down the Haast Pass to Queenstown for Doubtful Sound and a free adventure day, and back via Aoraki Mt Cook and Lake Tekapo. Three days have 5 to 6 hours of driving, and the Doubtful Sound day from Queenstown is about 12 hours; a scenic flight-cruise is a shorter option. We removed the original plan's second car pick-up in Queenstown: you keep the car from Christchurch throughout.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in New Zealand dollars, never in INR. Cards and contactless work almost everywhere.

good_to_know.title: Driving on the left
good_to_know.text: New Zealand drives on the left. Your Indian licence is accepted if it is in English; otherwise carry an approved translation or International Driving Permit. Roads are winding and one-lane bridges are common: slow down and give way as signed.

good_to_know.title: Four seasons in a day
good_to_know.text: Pack layers, a rain jacket and sunscreen. The UV index in New Zealand is very high even on cool days.

dining_intro: Auckland, Christchurch and Queenstown have many Indian and vegetarian restaurants; Rotorua and small towns have fewer. We send your diet to every hotel and tour in advance.
dining_avoid: Hāngī feasts are cooked with meat in an earth oven; ask for the vegetarian hāngī, which is cooked separately.
food_card: We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
